questions.subject: Unit 1 • The National Movement (1919–1935)
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of the Indian national movement in chronological order.
1. Gandhi–Irwin Pact
2. Poona Pact
3. Lahore Session of the Congress and the Purna Swaraj resolution
4. Announcement of the Communal Award
Choose the correct code:
questions.verificationSource: National Archives of India and Spectrum's Modern India
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: the Congress adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution at its Lahore session in December 1929 (3); Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin signed their pact on 5 March 1931 (1); British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award on 16 August 1932 (4); and Gandhi and Dr B. R. Ambedkar reached the Poona Pact on 24 September 1932 (2). The correct order is 3 – 1 – 4 – 2.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. The original explanation's dates and context should be checked against a reliable chronology.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • Revolutionary Movements in India and Abroad
questions.question: Who played a leading role in the formation of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) at Delhi's Feroz Shah Kotla grounds in September 1928?
options: Rash Behari Bose and Sachindra Nath Sanyal
Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla Khan
questions.verificationSource: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence
questions.explanation: The Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), formed in Kanpur in 1924, was reorganized after the Kakori case at a meeting held at Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi in September 1928. Chandrashekhar Azad was a key revolutionary leader, and Bhagat Singh proposed adding the word 'Socialist' to the organization's name. The HSRA adopted socialism as an explicit ideological objective.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Check the source's precise wording on who proposed the name and led the reorganization.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • Constitutional Development and Independence (1935–1947)
questions.question: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, who was given the power to allocate residuary legislative powers in the proposed federal system?
options: The Secretary of State for India
questions.verificationSource: Subhash Kashyap, Our Constitution, and M. Laxmikanth
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1935 divided legislative subjects among the Federal List, Provincial List and Concurrent List. Subjects outside these lists were treated as residuary matters. The Act did not simply assign them to the Federal Legislature or the provinces; Section 104 empowered the Governor-General to decide how such matters would be allocated, subject to the provisions of the Act.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Verify the exact statutory formulation and section reference against the Act.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • Prehistoric and Protohistoric Uttarakhand (State-Specific)
questions.question: Which prehistoric rock-art site in Uttarakhand, discovered by Dr Maheshwar Prasad Joshi in 1968 on the bank of the Suyal River, is associated with a rock formation shaped like a cobra's hood?
questions.verificationSource: Dr Yashwant Singh Katoche, The New History of Uttarakhand
questions.explanation: Lakhudiyar is located near Barachhina on the Almora–Bageshwar route, on the right bank of the Suyal River. The Hindi source credits historian Dr Maheshwar Prasad Joshi with its discovery in 1968. The rock shelter contains prehistoric paintings in red, white and black, including human figures, animals and geometric forms. The site name is commonly rendered in English as Lakhudiyar or Lakh-u-Udyar.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Confirm the discovery attribution, spelling, location and description from an authoritative Uttarakhand archaeology source.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • The Kuninda and Yaudheya Dynasties (State-Specific)
questions.question: Who was the most prominent ruler of the ancient Kuninda dynasty of Uttarakhand, whose silver and copper coins bear the legend in Prakrit and Kharoshthi: 'Rajnah Kunindasa Amoghabhutisa Maharajasa'?
questions.verificationSource: Dr Shiv Prasad Dabral 'Charan', History of Uttarakhand
questions.explanation: Amoghbhuti is regarded as a prominent ruler of the Kuninda dynasty. Coins attributed to him carry a legend identifying him as the great king of the Kunindas; examples feature symbols including a deer and the goddess Lakshmi. The script and exact reading of the legend should be described carefully because examples and scholarly readings can vary.
questions.reviewStatus: FACTUAL/EPIGRAPHIC REVIEW REQUIRED. The Hindi source's claim about the legend being in both Prakrit and Kharoshthi and its geographic extent needs expert verification.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • The Kartikeyapura (Katyuri) Dynasty (State-Specific)
questions.question: Which ruler of the Kartikeyapura dynasty is described in the Pandukeshwar and Bageshwar inscriptions as a Paramamaheshvara and as a builder of temples in the capital, and is said to have ruled contemporaneously with Pala ruler Dharmapala?
questions.verificationSource: Bageshwar, Pandukeshwar and Kandara copper-plate records; Dr Yashwant Singh Katoche
questions.explanation: The Hindi source identifies Ishtaganadeva of the Nimbara branch of the Kartikeyapura dynasty and associates him with Shaivism and temple building. It refers to the Bageshwar inscription and Pandukeshwar copper plates. Before publication, the proposed contemporaneity with Pala ruler Dharmapala and the named temple-building claims should be checked against the inscriptions and a specialist history of the Katyuris.
questions.reviewStatus: FACTUAL REVIEW REQUIRED. The source mixes several dynasty and inscription claims; verify them before treating this answer as definitive.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • The Chand Dynasty of Kumaon (State-Specific)
questions.question: Which Chand ruler of Kumaon met Mughal emperor Akbar at Lahore and is credited in the question with organizing land measurement and the revenue arrangements known as sirti and 'chhattis rakam battis kalam'?
questions.verificationSource: Badri Datt Pandey, History of Kumaon
questions.explanation: Rudra Chand (1568–1597 CE) is associated with diplomatic contact with Akbar and is said to have visited Lahore in 1587. The Hindi source's claims about the sirti revenue term and the 'chhattis rakam battis kalam' system need to be attributed precisely: its own explanation shifts some administrative reforms to Rudra Chand's successor Lakshmi Chand. The item should not be published until this mismatch has been resolved.
questions.reviewStatus: FACTUAL REVIEW REQUIRED. The question and explanation appear internally inconsistent about which Chand ruler introduced the revenue measures.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • The Parmar (Panwar) Dynasty of Garhwal (State-Specific)
questions.question:
Match List I (Parmar rulers of Garhwal) with List II (historical event or achievement).

List I
A. Ajaypal
B. Balbhadra Shah
C. Mahipati Shah
D. Pradyumna Shah

List II
1. The first Parmar ruler to assume the title 'Shah'
2. Unification of the 52 forts of Garhwal and the capitals at Devalgarh and Srinagar
3. Death while fighting the Gorkhas at the Battle of Khurbura (1804)
4. Campaign in Tibet (Dapa) and the commanders Madho Singh Bhandari and Lodi Rikhola

Choose the correct code:
questions.verificationSource: Harikrishna Raturi, History of Garhwal, and Dr Ajay Rawat
questions.explanation: The Hindi explanation associates Ajaypal with unifying the 52 forts and shifting the capital, Balbhadra Shah with the title 'Shah', Mahipati Shah with commanders Madho Singh Bhandari and Lodi Rikhola, and Pradyumna Shah with the 1804 Battle of Khurbura. This yields A–2, B–1, C–4, D–3, corresponding to option 4.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Confirm the identities, chronology and name spellings with specialist Uttarakhand history sources.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • Gorkha and British Rule in Uttarakhand (State-Specific)
questions.question: Following the Anglo-Gorkha War during Lord Hastings's tenure, when was the Treaty of Sugauli originally signed by Gorkha representative Gajraj Mishra and British representative Colonel Paris Bradshaw, and when was it ratified by the Nepalese court?
options: Signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816
Signed in April 1815 and ratified in December 1815
Signed in May 1814 and ratified in March 1815
Signed in January 1816 and ratified in August 1816
questions.verificationSource: Atkinson's Himalayan Gazetteer and Dr Shekhar Pathak
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Sugauli was signed on 2 December 1815 by representatives of the East India Company and Nepal. Nepal's formal ratification followed on 4 March 1816. The treaty resulted in Nepal ceding Kumaon and Garhwal, among other territories, to the British. The dates and the names/titles of the signatories should be checked against the treaty text and a reliable historical account.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Verify the treaty signatories and formal ratification details against a primary or authoritative source.

questions.subject: Unit 1 • The British Kumaon Commissionership (State-Specific)
questions.question: Which British Commissioner of Kumaon introduced the settlement in 1823 described in the source as the 'Assi Sala Bandobast' or the five-year land settlement of Vikram Samvat 1880, under which village boundaries were formally recorded for the first time?
questions.verificationSource: Kumaon Commission records and Dr R. S. Tolia, British Kumaon-Garhwal
questions.explanation: The Hindi source attributes the 1823 settlement to George William Traill, the second Commissioner of Kumaon, and describes it as a five-year settlement associated with Vikram Samvat 1880. It says the settlement recorded village boundaries and land. The unusual label 'Assi Sala Bandobast' and its relationship to a five-year settlement require checking against the cited regional history before the item is approved.
questions.reviewStatus: FACTUAL REVIEW REQUIRED. The source's name for the settlement and its stated duration appear potentially inconsistent.
